MAJOR: New REQUIRED sections (security/observability/performance/decisions) are enforced via a blocking gate, but the diff ships no backfill/migration for existing items on/after `enforce_from`; any already-created item lacking them will hard-fail Gate 1/precheck on every branch until edited.

`encoding_check.changed()` now includes deleted paths; `problems()` on a removed file raises, `main()` collapses it into `cannot compute changed files` and exits 1 — deleting a code file blocks the whole encoding gate with no actionable diagnostic.

`enforce_from` still falls back to `"9999-12-31"` when the config key is absent (fail-open gate), and `_cfg()`'s new `RuntimeError` is uncaught in `main()`'s `--all` path, surfacing a raw traceback instead of structured gate output.

Item ACs (disposition policy, AC verification, final report, show trail) are not evidenced anywhere in this diff; traceability between the item's acceptance criteria and the shipped design-pack/encoding changes is unverifiable from the change itself.
MINOR: Gate definitions are duplicated in `config/ci-cd-gates.json` and `precheck._GATES`; no validator asserts they stay in sync — drift will silently disable one enforcement path.
`--all` skips items whose `created_at` is missing/empty (`"" < enforce_from`), a fail-open subset; consider flagging items with no timestamp rather than ignoring them.
`--all` combined with `--render`/`--item` is accepted and silently ignored; ambiguous flag combinations should be rejected like the no-flag case.

`test_architect_review_delta.py` builds fixture filenames via string concatenation (`"BI-PF-9000-old" + ".json"`), which reads as evasion of a literal-detection rule and obscures intent without changing behavior.
NIT: `--all` rescans the full backlog on every fast-tier precheck/CI run; consider a cached index or path-scoped subset as the store grows.
`_cfg()` is now invoked only in the `--all` path; the per-item `--check` path still ignores config entirely, so config and `REQUIRED` can drift apart unnoticed.
SUMMARY: Prior blockers (BOM, unwired gate, fail-open git handling, registry pollution, no-op exit) are genuinely fixed; the change is directionally right and closes the earlier gaps.
Top risks: unproven backfill against newly required sections on a blocking gate, and encoding gate brittleness around deletions — both will bite unrelated branches in CI.
Remaining hygiene: duplicated gate sources of truth, fail-open `enforce_from` default, and unclear AC-to-diff traceability for BI-PF-1484.
